parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment begins with "3) detection heuristics for logical reasoning phenomena," where "3)" is the item number of the review comment itself, not a reference to a specific section or part of the paper. The comment does not explicitly mention any section, table, figure, or unique aspect of the paper, and its content touches on multiple technical points (detection heuristics, experimental comparisons with T5 baselines, and pre-training with logical reasoning phenomena), so the authors cannot confidently determine which specific part is being addressed. The comment does, however, specify what it considers problematic: it argues that none of the components alone is novel enough and that the pre-training approach amounts to a sententious logical relation extraction whose effectiveness was already demonstrated in reference [1], which is cited with full bibliographic details. Thus, while the specificity requirement regarding what needs to be addressed is met, the grounding is weak because the referenced part cannot be precisely identified.
